title: Three-view identity orbit
question: Can Gemini Omni hold one room's identity through continuous motion when conditioned on every Pass A–accepted still of that room at once?
one_way_note: A clean synthetic orbit is a best case for identity. Drift here damages the whole video probe. Parity with the still packet proves nothing about real capture.
operator_notes: Attach all three reference images in one generation. Do not generate from A-wide alone.
No complete four-view Pass A–accepted Omni packet exists yet; RP-014 is the strongest three-view set (A-wide, C-inventory, D-condition).
RP-014-B-reverse is not pass_a_accepted — do not attach it.
Not wired into build_video_tasks.py (VU-* only). Stage manually under video/google/gemini-omni/ if accepted.
wall: Development evidence only. Never present as a real walkthrough. Google arm excluded from publication and training (docs/31 B9).

intended_negatives: runner stripe is not a stain
continuity_must_hold: same cream walls, striped runner, entryphone and dark front door
door count and door positions never change
runner pattern and colour never morph
clips.exact_prompt: Create one continuous photorealistic video that looks like an ordinary handheld smartphone walkthrough of an entrance hall in a narrow communal-entry flat hallway with dated finishes. You are given three reference photographs of the SAME hall from different viewpoints. Match layout, fittings, finishes and lighting to those references; the A-wide image is the opening frame. Camera: hold the A-wide doorway framing for about one second, then walk slowly forward down the hall while gently orbiting the viewpoint so that by mid-take the entryphone and coat hooks from the inventory reference are clearly readable, and by the final two seconds a low condition detail of the runner edge and skirting matching the condition reference is in frame; one unbroken take; small natural handheld wobble only; no pause that feels like a cut. Visible evidence required across the take: hall walls, striped runner, coat hooks, entryphone, ceiling light, skirting, front door, shoe rack. Intended visible defects: none. Negative controls: runner stripe is not a stain; door shadow is not damp. The room is ordinarily occupied with coats and shoes under warm ceiling light without daylight. Hold fixed for the whole take: same cream walls, striped runner, entryphone and dark front door; door count and positions never change; runner pattern never morphs; no second doorway is invented. Audio: the clip is silent; no speech, no music, no sound effects, no room tone. Avoid: people, logos, readable text, watermark, impossible geometry, extra doors, scene cuts, dissolves or fades, speed ramps, slow motion, title cards, music, sound effects, camera-operator commentary, drone or crane moves, tripod-smooth motorised motion. Do not add labels, captions, borders, or inspection annotations. Show only visually supportable property evidence; do not make hidden areas visible.

gold.scored_by: Pass A strip continuity across 1 fps samples plus opening-frame match to A-wide; then optional segment+describe item recall against the union of the three accepted RP-014 stills under Pass B labels
fail_if: opening frame does not match A-wide
any fixture identity morphs between sampled frames
an extra door or room appears
